The Messerschmitt Me 262 was the world's first operational jet fighter, entering German service in 1944. Its 540 mph top speed made it nearly uncatchable, but engine reliability, fuel shortages, and late-war chaos limited its impact. 1,430 were built; its swept wings influenced all later jet design.
